database_summary: Retail / e‑commerce dataset (SQLite) containing customers, orders, order line items, payments, reviews, products, sellers, geolocation and two marketing leads tables. Mix of entity/dimension tables (customers, sellers, products, geolocation, product category translations), transactional/event tables (orders, order_items, order_payments, order_reviews) and marketing pipeline tables (leads_qualified, leads_closed). Row counts indicate orders ~99k, order_items ~112k (one-to-many to orders), products ~33k, geolocation large (many lat/lng per zip prefix).

accepted.name: orders_enriched_with_customer
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  orders.order_id,
  orders.customer_id,
  customers.customer_unique_id,
  customers.customer_zip_code_prefix,
  customers.customer_city,
  customers.customer_state,
  orders.order_status,
  orders.order_purchase_timestamp,
  orders.order_approved_at,
  orders.order_delivered_carrier_date,
  orders.order_delivered_customer_date,
  orders.order_estimated_delivery_date
FROM orders
LEFT JOIN customers
  ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id
accepted.description: One-row-per-order combining orders with customer demographic attributes (zip, city, state). Use when analyzing orders by customer geography or joining orders to geolocation or customer_unique_id. | Use for: orders by customer geography (state/city/zip); time-to-delivery or delivery lag by customer region; joining order-level data to payments/reviews/order_items later

accepted.name: order_items_with_product_and_seller
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  oi.order_id,
  oi.order_item_id,
  oi.product_id,
  products.product_category_name,
  oi.seller_id,
  sellers.seller_zip_code_prefix,
  sellers.seller_city,
  sellers.seller_state,
  oi.shipping_limit_date,
  oi.price,
  oi.freight_value,
  products.product_weight_g,
  products.product_length_cm,
  products.product_height_cm,
  products.product_width_cm
FROM order_items oi
LEFT JOIN products
  ON oi.product_id = products.product_id
LEFT JOIN sellers
  ON oi.seller_id = sellers.seller_id
accepted.description: One-row-per-order_item enriched with product and seller descriptive attributes. Useful for per-line revenue, seller performance, product-level analysis, and size/weight-based shipping analysis. | Use for: line-item revenue and freight analysis; seller-level sales and shipping performance; product dimension lookups for size/weight-based modeling

accepted.name: order_payments_agg_per_order
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_count,
  SUM(payment_value) AS payment_value_total,
  MIN(payment_type) AS payment_type_first,
  MAX(payment_installments) AS payment_installments_max
FROM order_payments
GROUP BY order_id
accepted.description: One-row-per-order aggregating payment rows into total payment value and counts. Use to compare paid amount to order-level totals or detect multi-part payments. | Use for: validate order payment completeness; analyze payment method distribution and installments; compare payment totals to order_items price sums

accepted.name: order_reviews_with_scores
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  review_id,
  order_id,
  review_score,
  review_comment_title,
  review_comment_message,
  review_creation_date,
  review_answer_timestamp
FROM order_reviews
accepted.description: One-row-per-review with normalized score and timestamps; preserves original review text. Use when analyzing ratings over time or mapping reviews to orders. | Use for: average review_score by product/seller/time; text analysis of review_comment_message/title; response time between review_creation_date and review_answer_timestamp

accepted.name: product_category_translations_norm
accepted.description: One-row-per-product_category_name with English translation. Use to map product category keys to readable English labels for reporting and joins to product dimension. | Use for: translate product category names for dashboards; grouping products by English category labels

accepted.name: geolocation_dedup_by_zip
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  AVG(geolocation_lat) AS geolocation_lat,
  AVG(geolocation_lng) AS geolocation_lng,
  MIN(geolocation_city) AS geolocation_city,
  MIN(geolocation_state) AS geolocation_state,
  COUNT(*) AS geolocation_point_count
FROM geolocation
GROUP BY geolocation_zip_code_prefix
accepted.description: One-row-per-zip-prefix selecting the centroid lat/lng and a representative city/state. Useful to join one coordinate per zip to customers/sellers without multiplying rows from multiple geolocation points. | Use for: map customers/sellers by zip centroid; distance calculations between customer and seller locations; visualization of sales density by geolocation

accepted.name: orders_with_customer_and_payment_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  c.customer_unique_id,
  c.customer_zip_code_prefix,
  c.customer_city,
  c.customer_state,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  o.order_approved_at,
  o.order_delivered_customer_date,
  COALESCE(p.payment_value_total,0.0) AS payment_value_total,
  COALESCE(p.payment_count,0) AS payment_count
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN customers c
  ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    COUNT(*) AS payment_count,
    SUM(payment_value) AS payment_value_total
  FROM order_payments
  GROUP BY order_id
) p
  ON o.order_id = p.order_id
accepted.description: One-row-per-order combining orders, customer attributes, and aggregated payments. Useful to validate paid amount vs orders and to analyze orders by customer and payment totals. | Use for: check orders with missing or partial payments; analyze order value distribution by customer region; correlate payment_count with fraud or churn signals

accepted.name: product_physical_dimensions
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  product_category_name,
  product_weight_g,
  product_length_cm,
  product_height_cm,
  product_width_cm,
  (COALESCE(product_length_cm,0.0) * COALESCE(product_height_cm,0.0) * COALESCE(product_width_cm,0.0)) AS product_volume_cm3,
  (COALESCE(product_length_cm,0.0) * COALESCE(product_width_cm,0.0)) AS product_area_cm2
FROM products
accepted.description: One-row-per-product with explicit physical volume and area measures derived from product dimensions. Useful for shipping cost models and dimensional analyses. | Use for: shipping cost estimation by dimensional weight; identify unusually large or heavy products; aggregate product volume by category

accepted.name: orders_latest_event_per_order
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  customer_id,
  order_status,
  order_purchase_timestamp,
  order_approved_at,
  order_delivered_carrier_date,
  order_delivered_customer_date,
  order_estimated_delivery_date,
  -- derive a single latest timestamp (string comparison works if format consistent)
  MAX(COALESCE(order_purchase_timestamp, '0000-00-00 00:00:00'),
      COALESCE(order_approved_at, '0000-00-00 00:00:00'),
      COALESCE(order_delivered_carrier_date, '0000-00-00 00:00:00'),
      COALESCE(order_delivered_customer_date, '0000-00-00 00:00:00'),
      COALESCE(order_estimated_delivery_date, '0000-00-00 00:00:00')) AS order_latest_event_timestamp,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY MAX(COALESCE(order_purchase_timestamp, '0000-00-00 00:00:00'),
                             COALESCE(order_approved_at, '0000-00-00 00:00:00'),
                             COALESCE(order_delivered_carrier_date, '0000-00-00 00:00:00'),
                             COALESCE(order_delivered_customer_date, '0000-00-00 00:00:00'),
                             COALESCE(order_estimated_delivery_date, '0000-00-00 00:00:00')) DESC) AS latest_event_rank
FROM orders
accepted.description: One-row-per-order exposing the latest non-null timestamp among order lifecycle columns and a rank of timestamp recency. Useful for latest-event analyses and top-recent-orders selection downstream by filtering on latest_event_rank. | Use for: find most recent orders; filter recent activity for monitoring dashboards; join latest order event timestamp to external data
